topomer.note: 22 of 88 molecules can be cut at the framework

findings.text: 40 chemotype(s); the largest holds 16 of 88 molecules -- a series of several scaffolds has no common frame, and an alignment will invent one
the common framework (framework of the largest chemotype) has 30 heavy atoms, about 83% of a typical molecule, and 25% of the set can be cut at it
the 30 shared framework atoms sit 0.0 A apart between molecules, over the best of their matches (22 of 88 carry them)
the aligned model is +0.564 in q2 against counts (95% interval +0.366 to +0.810) -- the frame does better than counts
the aligned model is +0.105 in q2 against invariant (95% interval -0.008 to +0.209) -- the frame gains nothing over invariant
the aligned model is +0.287 in q2 against topomer (95% interval -0.280 to +0.925) -- cutting the molecules and posing the pieces by rule does as well as the frame, on the molecules that can be cut
the aligned model is +0.559 in q2 against descriptors (95% interval +0.324 to +0.852) -- the geometry adds something

why: the frame carries signal and the molecules are superimposed, so a frame exists whoever made it; the several Murcko scaffolds only mean the program could not have built it, not that it is wrong
